In the window: hyperscaler Q3 calls (late Oct), where 2027 capex guides feed the AI-compute trade and my price-path view (higher capex = more 2027-28 supply); Nvidia's results (~19 Nov); possible Tesla-SpaceX merger news before Tesla's annual meeting (Barclays: before December, with a two-board approval hurdle); Starship Flight 15, which Musk puts 'just before Thanksgiving', so probably just after the window (Manifold ~36% for a ship catch). The IPO lock-up (~180 days, ~Dec 9) falls just after the window and may weigh into late November. Net: roughly symmetric around $152.5, sigma ~19% (realized 82% inflated after IPO, so ~65% annual / 3.5).

reasoning: Industry lane. (1) Reported base: Q3-26 revenue $14.6B, SI $7.6B, 1.7 GW, Q4 capex guide $35-40B (~2x the Aug guide), Q1-27 revenue guide $33-37B, net cash $51B, 13.58B shares. (2) Shortage durability, from the value chain: new-chip rent is ~$50/W-yr (CFO, Nebius $40-50M/MW short-term), the B300 index is at a record (Oct-26) and the H100 index is +40% since Oct-25, so pricing holds into mid-2027. But hyperscaler capex steps to ~$1.0-1.3T in 2027, CoWoS goes to ~200k wpm, and the last shortage (H100 2023-24) ended with a ~64% price drop within ~18 months. Power (38 GW shortfall, turbine slots to 2029-30) is the one constraint that argues for longer. My path: $52 (2026), $50 in H1-27 falling to $44 in H2-27, $35 (2028), $27, $23, then the NPV-0 price of $18.1 from 2031. The shortage lasts about 18 months from today at full strength and fades over 2028-30. (3) Capacity: 8 GW at YE27, not 13. Delivered +0.3-0.4 GW a quarter in Q2-Q3; 13 GW needs 2.6 GW a quarter and ~$383B of 2027 SI capex. JPM models 10 GW and MS 8.3 GW. (4) Kilian's SOTP: fleet run-off at spot $378B, build window $20B, Starlink DCF $264B, Space $70B, Cursor $55B, X $10B, less 10% holdco, gives $45.8/sh. The multiple legs at 10x EBITDA and 20x P/E give $93.3 and $86.9, and the engine blends to $73.0 (with Kilian's 15x/27x it would be ~$98). (5) The ladder does not jump to fair value. 12-month price changes are close to a random walk and narrative stocks can stay rich, so I centre the distribution on ~$125 (bear $72 at 30%, base $130 at 45%, bull $225 at 25%), with ~27-30% dispersion within each scenario. That gives P(>= $152) = 0.35, against ~0.45 for a driftless lognormal.

model_inputs.structure_note: Value is carried by Kilian's three legs: 0.4 consolidated EV/EBITDA (10x NTM GAAP EBITDA), 0.4 SOTP (fleet run-off at spot by vintage, 2029-30 build window, Starlink subscriber DCF, Space tree, Cursor and X marks, 10% holdco discount), 0.2 P/E (20x NTM GAAP EPS). model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) Multiples set below his 15x EV/EBITDA and 27x P/E. Horizon NTM EBITDA is ~85% compute rent at ~2x the NPV-0 new-chip price ($18.1/W-yr at $36/W capex), earned by a fleet with a 6-year life. My SOTP is worth ~5x that EBITDA, so 15x would require the shortage to persist indefinitely. With 15x and 27x, fair value is ~$98 instead of ~$73 (a departure of more than 5%). (2) Net debt at the horizon is stated directly ($51B) from a quarterly build; the engine's linear proration would understate the Q4-26 and 2027 burn. (3) EchoStar is charged as 261.8M added shares plus $8.5B cash, not inside the Starlink part, so it is not counted twice. (4) The SOTP leg sits ~45% below the multiple legs; the gap is the 'durability' question itself.
